question_text: Table 1 shows tax collection (in million pesos) for three cities: City X: 500, City Y: 700, City Z: 600. Table 2 shows population density (people per sq km) for the same cities: City X: 2,000, City Y: 3,500, City Z: 1,500. Which city has the highest tax collection per person? (Assume population = density × area, but area is unknown. However, tax per person can be compared using tax/density if area is same? Actually, we need to find tax per capita. Since area is not given, we cannot compute exact per capita. But if we assume area is the same for all cities, then tax per person is proportional to tax/density. Compute tax/density: City X: 500/2000 = 0.25; City Y: 700/3500 = 0.20; City Z: 600/1500 = 0.40. So City Z has the highest.)
